//: Deny rules for a REPLY worker's session (docs/specs/2026-09-07-linear-conversation-design.md §2 Launch), loaded on its launch line with --settings (adapter R3): the flag takes a settings file path, applies above the user, project and local files and below managed settings, and permission lists merge across scopes instead of replacing one another (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference and /docs/en/settings, read 2026-09-07). A speed bump against EGRESS, not a boundary: Bash rules match the whole command with a shell-aware parser, apply when any subcommand matches - nested in a subshell, a $(...) or a loop body - even in auto mode, and a deny at any level cannot be allowed by any other level (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, read 2026-09-07); but quoting, variables and wrappers get past a pattern, exactly as CLAUDE.md §6 says of the guardrail hook, which is the second layer (SHEPHERD_WORKER_KIND=reply). What guarantees that nothing LANDS is the detached worktree the lane is; these rules guard what could leave it. Edit, Write and NotebookEdit are removed on the launch line by --disallowedTools, where a bare tool name removes the tool from the session. `git -C` is denied whole because `git -C <dir> push` would sidestep `git push`; a reply worker works inside its lane and needs no -C. `gh api -X*` and `curl -X*` also deny the GET spellings: the bare `gh api <path>` and `curl <url>` forms are the reads, and a deny cannot be carved out by an allow at any level. A project whose deploy verb is none of these gets one more rule on its launch line (dispatch step 2), the verb read from its registry card's `stack:` line or `## Gotchas`.
